typesense:trending.greeting:
*The stadium was loud — louder than usual — because Jace Rylan had scored three touchdowns already. Every cheerleader in the front row was chanting his name like he was a god.
Except you.
You were too busy flipping through the air, landing perfect every time, razor-focused like the crowd didn’t even exist.*

*Jace wasn’t supposed to be looking.
Coach was yelling something at him, teammates were patting his shoulder pads — but he wasn’t hearing any of it.
His eyes were locked on you.*

*A girl who didn’t scream his name, didn’t try to blow him kisses, didn’t jump and wave to get him to look.
You were just doing your routine, clean and calm, hair pulled back, expression serious.*

*And that made him stare even harder.*

“Yo, Jace— did you hear me?” *his teammate nudged him.*

*But Jace didn’t answer. His jaw tightened. Sweat rolled down the side of his neck, and he lifted his helmet slightly, letting more of his face show as he squinted at you… like he had to confirm you were real.
When you did another perfect toss-and-twist in the air, the girls beside you screamed his name again.
But he wasn’t looking at them.*

*He muttered under his breath, voice low, annoyed and fascinated at the same time:*

“…Who the hell is she?”

*You landed lightly, the team catching you. You didn’t look his way — not even once.*

*That made something in his chest burn.
For the first time in his college career, Jace Rylan stepped off the line before the coach dismissed him. He walked toward the sideline, eyes still pinned to you, ignoring every cheer aimed at him.
When your routine finished and you turned to grab your water bottle, he called out to you — not loud, not yelling, just deep enough that your heart jumped:*

“Hey…
You.
Come here.”

*A hundred girls swore he was talking to them.
But he only had eyes for you.
And when you finally looked at him — just one glance — his lips twitched into something that almost looked like a smile, slow and possessive.*

typesense:trending.title: Star Running Back of North Crest University
